title: Building Density and Setbacks for Houses under QCVN 01:2026 (2027)
desc: QCVN 01:2026/BXD from 1 January 2027: maximum building density for single-family houses by plot area, setback table by road width, notes on existing areas.
summary: Summary of the building density, setback and plot dimension indicators for single-family houses in QCVN 01:2026/BXD, the new planning standard effective from 1 January 2027.
body: The Ministry of Construction has issued QCVN 01:2026/BXD, the national technical regulation on urban and rural planning, together with Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD. The regulation takes effect on 1 January 2027 and replaces QCVN 01:2021/BXD. Until the end of 2026 the new regulation is not yet in force; this article helps homeowners prepare.
Net building density: the percentage ratio between the ground footprint of buildings on the plot and the plot area.
Land use coefficient: the ratio (in times) between total floor area (including basements, excluding technical, fire-protection, refuge and parking floors) and the site area.
Red line (chỉ giới đường đỏ): the boundary between the land that may be built on and the land reserved for roads, infrastructure and public space.
Building line: the limit within which a building may be built above ground. The setback is the space between the red line and the building line.
2. Maximum building density for single-family houses
Table 8 in Section 2.5.3.1 sets the maximum net building density by plot area (m² per house); existing areas also use this table (Section 2.6.6.1), except in the case described in section 4 below:

The land use coefficient of a single-family house plot must not exceed 7 times; a house combined with other functions must additionally meet fire protection and environmental hygiene requirements. In rural areas, if agricultural land is attached to the house, the plot area includes this land.
3. Setbacks by road width and building height
Table 7 in Section 2.5.2 applies to sites adjoining roads of area-level or higher (minimum setback, in metres):
Road width under 19 m: building under 19 m high - 0; from 19 to under 22 m - 3; from 22 to under 28 m - 4; from 28 m - 6.
Road width 19 to under 22 m: building under 22 m high - 0; from 22 to under 28 m - 3; from 28 m - 6.
Road width 22 m or more: building under 28 m high - 0; from 28 m - 6.

According to the table, a building under 19 m high has a minimum setback of 0 at every road width; the specific setback of each site is still set by the detailed plan or urban design (Section 2.5.2.1).
4. New development areas and existing areas

New development areas: the road frontage of a single-family house plot must be no less than 5 m if the road's red line width is 19 m or more, and no less than 4 m if the road is under 19 m (Section 2.5.6).

Existing areas: a single-family house plot no higher than 25 m and no larger than 100 m² may be built to 100% density, but must still ensure setbacks and distances (Section 2.6.6.2). Where the general setback cannot be met, the detailed plan or urban design may set a different setback, but it must be uniform along the street (Section 2.6.4).
5. Balconies, canopies and the neighbouring house

Architectural details projecting beyond the building line must not go past the red line (where there is a setback) and must not obstruct traffic, pedestrians on the pavement or fire engines. The part adjoining the neighbouring house must not cross the plot boundary and must not adversely affect the neighbouring building's living conditions (Sections 2.5.7 and 2.5.8).
6. Do old plans have to be redone?

Plans approved before 1 January 2027 continue to be implemented until their term ends; if adjusted after that date, they must follow the new regulation (Section 5.4). The regulation is a tool for state agencies to control planning; the indicators applying to your plot are in the detailed plan, urban design and building permit; see Procedure for a building permit for a single-family house in 2026.

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. QCVN 01:2026/BXD (Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD) is not yet in force and applies from 1 January 2027; before then QCVN 01:2021/BXD still applies (its full text is not yet in our library). The specific indicators for each plot are determined by the approved plan.
